# Temple Scroll Column 13 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 13 | **Condition:** fragmentary

---

**13:1** [...] On the fifteenth day of the seventh month [...]

**13:2** [...] when you have gathered the produce of the land [...]

**13:3** [...] you shall celebrate a festival to the LORD for seven days [...]

**13:4** [...] On the first day there shall be a sacred assembly; you shall do no laborious work [...]

**13:5** [...] It is the Festival of Booths, seven days to the LORD [...]

**13:6** [...] You shall present a burnt offering, an offering by fire of pleasing aroma to the LORD [...]

**13:7** [...] thirteen young bulls from the herd, two rams, fourteen yearling lambs without blemish [...]

**13:8** [...] with their grain offerings and drink offerings for the bulls, the rams, and the lambs [...]

**13:9** [...] according to their number, as prescribed [...]

**13:10** [...] and one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the perpetual burnt offering [...]

**13:11** [...] its grain offering and its drink offering [...]

**13:12** [...] And you shall dwell in booths for seven days [...]

**13:13** [...] Every native-born in Israel shall dwell in booths [...]

**13:14** [...] so that your generations may know that I made the children of Israel dwell in booths [...]

**13:15** [...] when I brought them out of the land of Egypt [...]

**13:16** [...] And you shall rejoice before Me for seven days — a perpetual statute throughout your generations [...]

---

*LOGOS notes: Column 13 is fragmentary but preserves the essential Festival of Booths (Sukkot) legislation, paralleling Numbers 29:12-16 and Leviticus 23:33-43. The first day's offering of thirteen bulls begins the distinctive descending sequence (13, 12, 11... 7) over the seven days. The theological rationale — dwelling in booths as an Exodus memorial — follows Leviticus 23:42-43. "Festival of Booths" is the standard scholarly rendering of chag ha-sukkot.*
